steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Test with a fake clock** in *Good tests: parametrize, fixtures and fakes*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: failures = [(n, want) for n, want in CASES if is_even(n) != want]

steps.title: Rebuild Test with a fake clock cold
prompt: `greeting(clock)` returns `"Good morning"` before 12:00, `"Good afternoon"` from 12:00 to 17:59, and `"Good evening"` from 18:00. It asks `clock.hour()` for the current hour, so tests can pass a fake.

Write a class `FakeClock(hour)` whose `hour()` returns the given hour, and at least three `test_` functions using it. Test the boundaries (11, 12, 17, 18). **Run checks** runs your tests against a correct `greeting` and broken ones.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
